questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the crossing guard says something different.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic light, red is always on top and green is always on the bottom. On a horizontal traffic light, red is always on the left and green is always on the right.

questions.question: You may turn right on red if you:

options.text: Stop first and check for traffic and pedestrians.
Are facing a red arrow.
Are in the left lane.
Slow down first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop first and check for traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You can turn right at a red light unless a sign says you cannot. You must stop completely first. Then check for pedestrians and other traffic before turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You may make left turns.
You may make U-turns.
You may pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: This sign shows a lane that is only for left-turning vehicles. You cannot use this lane to pass other cars or drive straight through.

questions.question: As you near an intersection, the traffic light changes from green to yellow. Your best action is to:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Get ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Try to move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Look at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: When an aggressive driver is behind you, move out of their way. Do not look at them. Do not speed up or block them, as this could make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must:

options.text: Stop five feet away from the bus.
Stop only if you see children are present.
Stop and remain stopped until it appears safe to proceed.
Stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and a stop arm extended, you must stop at least 10 feet away. Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing, the stop arm is withdrawn, and children have reached a safe place. This applies whether you approach from behind, from the front, or at an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection and have a green light. Pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if they are crossing against the red light. Protect pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down on a highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Carefully drive off the road as far as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car is broken down.

questions.question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly from your current lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.explanation: Use hand signals to show when you are turning if your turn signals do not work.

questions.question: If your blood alcohol level is 0.04 percent, what is true?

options.text: You are two to seven times more likely to crash than someone who has not drunk alcohol.
You are above the legal limit but fine to drive.
You can drive safely.
You should drink coffee before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are two to seven times more likely to crash than someone who has not drunk alcohol.
questions.explanation: No amount of alcohol is safe before driving. Even at 0.04 percent blood alcohol, which is below the legal limit for adults 21 and older, you are two to seven times more likely to crash than someone with no alcohol in their blood.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring straight ahead at the road for a long time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep the night before.
Driving short distances on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring straight ahead at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead for a long time and stop looking ahead, behind, and around your vehicle. You may zone out and not notice traffic slowing or stopping ahead.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes on an interstate, signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot. Only stop on the shoulder for emergencies. Change lanes as rarely as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell.
Let it go and move on.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off in return.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go and move on.
questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and continue driving safely.

questions.question: If a truck swings left before turning right, what is dangerous to do?

options.text: Try to squeeze between the truck and the curb to turn right.
Brake until the truck finishes turning.
Break the four-second following distance rule.
Honk your horn at the truck driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to squeeze between the truck and the curb to turn right.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need wide space to turn. A truck that swings left may actually be turning right. It is dangerous to pass a turning truck or squeeze between the truck and the curb. The truck driver cannot see vehicles in that space.

questions.question: What is the main cause of traffic deaths in work zones?

options.text: Tire blowouts.
Hydroplaning from water on the road.
Loss of steering control from wet paint.
Carelessness and speeding.

questions.explanation: Carelessness and speeding are the main causes of traffic deaths in work zones.
